title: Import the test harness from bun:test

facts.note: Test files only; the detector scans exactly these globs, whatever the file's language.
File belongs to a Bun stack: workspace provider capability `atdd.workspace.bun` with declared `runtime.runner` = `bun`. Needs a workspace-capability observer.

fires: A test file in a Bun workspace is created or edited (the harness must come from `bun:test`).
A test file in a Bun workspace imports `describe/expect/it` from `vitest`.
A `*.spec.*` file in a Bun workspace requires `chai` or `mocha`, or imports `@jest/globals`.
A test kept on a foreign runner during a migration is still in the tree.
doesNotFire: A non-test source file imports a foreign harness (different smell, not scanned).
A test file in a workspace whose provider is not `atdd.workspace.bun`.

given: A test file (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`) in a Bun stack whose workspace provider declares `bun` as the runner
when: the test file is written or changed
then: Import its harness from `bun:test`; never import `vitest`, `jest`, `@jest/globals`, `mocha` or `chai`.
prefer: Import the harness from Bun: `import { describe, expect, it } from "bun:test";` — Jest-compatible assertions, so usually only the import line changes.
avoid: `import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";` — not run by the declared runner.
Expecting a test kept on a foreign runner during migration to be exempt: it stays reported until it moves; the finding is the migration's explicit, reviewable open item.
Toolchain sprawl: a foreign runner and transform pipeline in a toolchain premised on Bun running TypeScript directly.
unless: The file is not a test file (a different smell, not scanned).
why: This rule is strict because the ATDD cost exceeds sprawl: acceptance tests are the evidence a phase gate consumes, reported in terms of its declared runner; a foreign-harness test is coverage the gate believes ran but never did — a green gate with an unexercised acceptance. A test the gate cannot run is worse than no test.
evidence: No test file (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`) imports or requires `vitest`, `jest`, `@jest/globals`, `mocha` or `chai`; harness imports come from `bun:test`.
`bun test` executes the acceptance tests and the bun_tester_discipline_detector reports zero findings.
verifier_detail: Zero-dependency Bun detector; scans TEST FILES ONLY (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*` — the only place a harness import belongs); non-test files are never scanned.
Masks line comments so a migration note naming the old runner does not trip it.
Does NOT mask string literals: the harness name lives inside the import's own string literal, so masking literals would blank the very thing being matched.
Flags any import or require of a foreign harness: `vitest`, `jest`, `@jest/globals`, `mocha`, `chai` (frameworks that drag their own runner and transform pipeline back in).
declared_runner: the `runtime.runner` provided by capability `atdd.workspace.bun` — `bun`; it is what the binding plan resolves and what the phase gate reports as having executed.
No per-rule scope in atdd-bun: a test deliberately retained on a foreign runner during migration stays reported until it moves.
Disposition strict, severity 2: every finding fails.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.

Bun-stack realization of the agnostic "the declared runner is the runner that runs" / "tests run on the declared runner" obligation, enforced by the `bun_fullstack_detector` family implementation on `atdd.workspace.bun`.

additions.text: Coder-facing text kept slightly above ~1,000 characters.
additions.justification: Lossless placement of the strict rationale, migration non-exemption and toolchain-sprawl cost requires it.

trace.note: Activates on any test file in a Bun stack, not only on existing harness imports.
Not a waiver: states that migration tests remain reported.
